recommendation_summary: The reply recommends having nightly-sync touch a timestamp file as its very first step, plus one small cron job that checks the file is fresh by 03:10 and alerts the user by NAS notification or separate email if it is not.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You want to know within hours if nightly-sync fails, without reading logs.
labels.Deleted: A centralized log stack (Synology + Docker, Pieter Levels style) — nothing today needs log aggregation, only this one job needs a failure alert.
labels.Bottleneck: nightly-sync can die before it reaches the email step, so the only signal you have never fires on failure.
labels.Checked myself: You told me it crashed at startup for four nights straight, before the email step, and nothing else alerts on this job.

note: The reply recommends a single heartbeat or dead-man check with no Docker or log server; the alert channel choice is one mechanism, not two.
